articles.title: Typhoon Day
articles.text:
Last night, the news said a typhoon was coming. This morning, the sky turned dark gray, and the wind grew strong. Dad moved the plants inside, and Mom filled some bottles with water. I helped tape the windows.
By noon, the rain was falling hard. The trees outside danced left and right in the wind. We could not go anywhere, so we stayed in the living room together. Mom made hot noodle soup. Dad told us stories about the big typhoons when he was young. My sister and I played cards and listened to the rain.
The power went out for one hour at night, so we lit candles. It was a little scary but also special. A typhoon day is not fun for everyone, but staying safe and warm with my family made me feel lucky.

What did Mom make at noon?
What happened at night?
options: The power went out for one hour.
A tree fell on the house.
questions.answer: The power went out for one hour.

articles.title: Packing for the Big Trip
articles.text:
Tomorrow, my family is going to Taitung for three days. Tonight, we are all packing. This is my first time packing my own backpack, and it is harder than I thought!
At first, I wanted to bring everything: five T-shirts, my games, three books, and my soccer ball. But my backpack is small. Mom laughed and said, "We are going for three days, not three months!"
So I made a list. Clothes for three days, a hat, my water bottle, sunscreen, and one book for the train ride. Dad checked our train tickets on his phone and printed a map of the town. My sister packed her camera. She wants to take one hundred photos of the sea.
Now my backpack is light and ready by the door. I can't sleep. I keep thinking about the blue sea and the hot spring. Taitung, here we come!

articles.title: The Train to Taitung
articles.text:
Our train left the city at nine in the morning. I love riding trains because you can see so much from the window.
First, we passed tall buildings and busy roads. Then, little by little, the view changed. We saw green rice fields, small towns, and long rivers. After two hours, the best part came: the sea! The water was so blue that everyone on the train said "Wow!" at the same time.
A grandma sat next to us. She was going home to Taitung. She shared some rice cakes with us and told us about the best places to eat there. "Try the fried rice noodles at the old market," she said. "My friend has sold them for forty years."
We arrived at one thirty. The air smelled like the sea. Our vacation finally started, and I already loved Taitung before we left the station.

What made everyone on the train say "Wow"?
options: The blue sea outside the window.
questions.answer: The blue sea outside the window.

options: The fried rice noodles at the old market.
The hot spring near the station.
The rice cakes at her home.

articles.title: A Day at the Beach
articles.text:
Today was our beach day in Taitung! The weather was perfect — sunny with a soft wind. We put on sunscreen, wore our hats, and walked to the beach after breakfast.
The sand was already warm under our feet. My sister and I ran into the water first. The waves pushed us and we laughed and shouted. Dad tried to surf on a small board, but he fell again and again. Even the lifeguard laughed!
After lunch, we rested under a big umbrella. I collected shells with my sister. She found a white shell that looks like a little fan. We also built a sandcastle with a bridge and a wall around it. A big wave came and washed half of it away, but we didn't care.
Before dinner, we watched the sky turn orange and pink. I took a photo with my heart, not my phone. I will remember this day forever.

What happened when Dad tried to surf?
options: He taught the kids to surf.

options: A white shell that looks like a little fan.
questions.answer: A white shell that looks like a little fan.

articles.title: Up the Mountain
articles.text:
On our last day in Taitung, we drove up a mountain to see the sunrise. We got up at four in the morning! I was sleepy, but Dad said, "Trust me, it will be worth it."
The mountain road had many turns. When we arrived at the top, the sky was still dark, and the air was cool. We drank hot milk tea and waited. Slowly, the sky turned from black to deep blue, then to gold. Finally, the sun jumped out of the sea of clouds. The view was so beautiful that nobody said a word.
On the way down, we stopped at a small waterfall and crossed an old bridge. The water was ice-cold and clear. We put our feet in and screamed — then laughed.
Dad was right. Getting up early was hard, but that golden morning was the best part of our whole trip.

What did they do while waiting for the sunrise?

options: At a small waterfall and an old bridge.
At a temple on the top.
questions.answer: At a small waterfall and an old bridge.

articles.title: The Old Temple Town
articles.text:
Have you ever visited Tainan? My classmate Emma went there last month, and she can't stop talking about it.
Tainan is one of the oldest cities in Taiwan. Emma visited a famous temple that is over three hundred years old. The roof has beautiful dragons, and the doors have paintings of old heroes. Her grandma taught her how to pray and told her the stories behind the temple.
But Emma's favorite part was the food. The old streets near the temple are full of small food stands. She ate shrimp rolls, tofu pudding, and fruit ice. "Everything was cheap and delicious," she said. "My stomach was so happy!"
Emma took a photo in front of the temple with her grandma. She keeps it on her desk now. "A city with old stories feels warm," she says. I want to visit Tainan this August, too.

What was Emma's favorite part of the trip?
What does Emma keep on her desk?
options: A photo with her grandma in front of the temple.
A dragon toy from the temple.
questions.answer: A photo with her grandma in front of the temple.

articles.title: Home Sweet Home
articles.text:
Our Taitung trip ended yesterday. When the train arrived back in our city, it was raining. We were tired, and our backpacks were heavy with dirty clothes and gifts.
But when we opened the door of our home, something felt wonderful. "Home sweet home!" Mom said. My own bed, my own desk, even the old sofa — everything looked friendly, like they were saying, "Welcome back!"
At dinner, we looked at our photos and laughed again at Dad's surfing. My sister chose her best sea photo and set it as the wallpaper on Mom's phone. I put my little shell on my bookshelf.
Dad asked, "So, where should we go next summer?" Everyone started talking at the same time — the mountains! An island! A big city! We couldn't agree, but it didn't matter. A trip gives you stories, and home gives you rest. We are lucky to have both.
